chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said:

I said to him, 'A man performing Tamattu' with Umrah until Hajj, in his bag are his clothes. Does he sell from his clothes and buy his sacrificial animal (Hady) from them?' He said, 'No. This is what the Believer adorns himself with. He should fast and not take anything from his clothes.'

key_terms.الْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ: Umrah until Hajj (the phrase indicating Tamattu' type)
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performing Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mu'tamir who sells his clothes to buy his Hajj sacrifice?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the garments used for Hajj are considered personal adornment and should not be liquidated to cover the cost of the sacrificial animal (Hady). Instead, the believer retains his clothes and fulfills the obligation through fasting, highlighting a practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the preservation of personal property during pilgrimage rituals.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to himasws, ‘A man performing Tumatto with the Umra to the Hajj and in his bag are his clothes. Is it for him that he sells his clothes and buys his sacrificial animal (from its proceeds)?’ Heasws said: ‘No. This is what the Believers adorns himself with. He should Fast and not take anything from his clothes’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous), and has clothes in his bag; if he can sell them and buy offering animal from the sale of the clothes.
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, believers dress up with clothes. He must fast and must not take anything from his clothes.”’
